Research question: 'How do sharks find their prey?'

Passage: 'Sharks are ancient predators that have lived on Earth for over 400 million years. They can detect tiny electrical signals given off by other animals using special sensors called the ampullae of Lorenzini. Sharks also have a lateral line system — a series of pressure-sensing organs along their sides — that detects movement and vibrations in the water. A shark can smell a drop of blood diluted in one million gallons of water. Sharks must keep swimming to breathe. The whale shark is the largest fish in the world.'

(a) Which fact from the passage MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) The ampullae of Lorenzini (electrical signal detection) and the lateral line (vibration detection) most directly answer how sharks find prey. Detecting blood smell is also very relevant. (b) 'Sharks have lived 400 million years' — about history, not hunting; 'whale shark is largest fish' — about size, not hunting. (c) Sample: 'How far away can a shark smell blood?' or 'Do all shark species hunt the same way?'

steps: (a) Read the question: how do sharks FIND prey? Focus on senses and detection.
Ampullae of Lorenzini (electrical signals): directly a prey-finding adaptation.
Lateral line (vibrations in water): directly a prey-finding adaptation.
Smell of blood: also prey-finding.
(b) 400 million years on Earth: history, not a prey-finding method.
Whale shark is largest fish: size fact, irrelevant to hunting.
(c) A good follow-up adds depth: how far, how fast, which sense is strongest?

Research question: 'What causes an earthquake?'

Passage: 'Earth's outer layer is broken into large pieces called tectonic plates that slowly move. When two plates grind against each other, pressure builds up over time. When the pressure is released suddenly, energy travels through the ground as seismic waves, which we feel as an earthquake. The point underground where an earthquake starts is called the focus; the point on the surface directly above it is the epicenter. Japan experiences thousands of earthquakes each year. The Richter scale is used to measure earthquake strength.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) Tectonic plates grinding build pressure, which releases suddenly as seismic waves felt as an earthquake — this most directly answers the cause. (b) 'Japan experiences thousands of earthquakes per year' — about frequency/location, not cause; 'The Richter scale measures strength' — about measurement, not cause. (c) Sample: 'What should I do when an earthquake happens?' or 'How deep underground do earthquakes start?'

steps: (a) The cause: tectonic plate grinding builds pressure; sudden release creates seismic waves.
(b) Japan's earthquake frequency: where/how often, not why earthquakes happen.
Richter scale: a measurement tool, not the cause.
(c) Good follow-ups extend understanding: safety, depth, prediction, effects.

Research question: 'How do Arctic foxes survive the cold winters?'

Passage: 'Arctic foxes live in some of the coldest places on Earth, where temperatures can drop to minus 58 degrees Fahrenheit. Their fur changes color from brown in summer to thick white fur in winter, which provides excellent camouflage in the snow. An Arctic fox's thick winter coat is so well insulated that the fox does not begin to shiver until temperatures fall below minus 94 degrees Fahrenheit. Arctic foxes also dig into snow drifts to shelter from blizzards. Their small, rounded ears and compact body shape reduce heat loss. Arctic foxes eat lemmings, birds, and carrion.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) The thick winter coat insulated enough to prevent shivering until minus 94 degrees, plus small rounded ears and compact body that reduce heat loss, most directly answer how Arctic foxes survive cold. (b) 'Their fur turns white in winter' — this fact is more about camouflage than warmth; 'Arctic foxes eat lemmings, birds, and carrion' — about diet, not cold survival. (c) Sample: 'How do Arctic fox pups survive their first winter?' or 'What do Arctic foxes eat when prey is scarce in winter?'

steps: (a) Thick insulated coat (shivering threshold at -94F): directly about surviving cold.
Small ears and compact body reducing heat loss: directly about surviving cold.
(b) White fur camouflage: survival benefit but about hiding from predators, less about warmth.
Diet (lemmings, birds): about food, not temperature survival.
(c) Strong follow-ups narrow to a specific related gap: pup survival, winter food scarcity.

Research question: 'How do honeybees communicate to tell each other where food is?'

Passage: 'When a worker bee finds a good source of flowers, she returns to the hive and performs a "waggle dance" — a figure-eight movement on the honeycomb. The direction of the dance indicates the direction of the food relative to the sun. The length of the waggle run tells other bees how far away the food is. Bees also use scent signals to communicate. A bee colony can have up to 60,000 bees. Worker bees live only about six weeks in summer. Honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs, still edible after 3,000 years.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) The waggle dance — its direction indicating food direction relative to the sun and waggle run length indicating distance — most directly answers how bees communicate about food location. (b) 'Worker bees live about six weeks in summer' — about lifespan, not communication; 'Honey has been found in Egyptian tombs still edible after 3,000 years' — about honey preservation, not bee communication. (c) Sample: 'Can bees use the waggle dance at night or when it is cloudy?' or 'What do bees do if the food source disappears?'

steps: (a) Waggle dance details (direction = food direction; run length = distance): both parts directly answer the question.
(b) Worker bee lifespan: about biology, not communication.
Ancient honey: about honey science, not bee communication.
(c) Good follow-ups probe limits or extensions of the dance behavior.

Research question: 'Why is the rainforest important to life on Earth?'

Passage: 'Rainforests cover only about 6% of Earth's land surface but produce more than 20% of the world's oxygen through photosynthesis. More than half of all plant and animal species on Earth live in rainforests, making them the most biodiverse ecosystems on the planet. Rainforest plants have been used to develop about 25% of all modern medicines. The Amazon rainforest absorbs billions of tons of carbon dioxide each year, helping to slow climate change. The Amazon River, which flows through the Amazon rainforest, is the largest river in the world by volume. Rainforests typically receive between 80 and 400 inches of rain per year.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) The Amazon absorbing billions of tons of CO2 to slow climate change, and rainforests producing 20% of Earth's oxygen, most directly answer why rainforests are important to all life on Earth. (b) 'The Amazon River is the largest by volume' — about river geography, not forest importance; 'Rainforests receive 80 to 400 inches of rain per year' — about rainfall amount, not why rainforests are important. (c) Sample: 'What would happen to Earth's climate if all rainforests were cut down?' or 'Which rainforest medicines have been discovered so far?'

steps: (a) Oxygen production (20%) and CO2 absorption: directly explain life-supporting functions.
Biodiversity (half of all species): another direct answer about ecological importance.
Medicines (25% derived from rainforest plants): another direct answer.
(b) Amazon River size: geographical, not about importance to life.
Rainfall amount: describes the ecosystem's weather, not its importance.
(c) Follow-ups could explore consequences of loss or specific benefits.

Research question: 'How do astronauts exercise in space?'

Passage: 'In space, there is no gravity to work against, so muscles and bones can weaken quickly without exercise. Astronauts on the International Space Station exercise for about two hours every day. They use a treadmill with a harness system that pushes them against the belt so they can run even without gravity. They also ride a stationary bike and use a resistance machine similar to weight lifting. Without regular exercise, astronauts could lose up to 20% of their muscle mass on a six-month mission. The International Space Station orbits Earth at about 17,500 miles per hour. Astronauts on the ISS see 16 sunrises per day.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) The description of specific exercise methods (harness treadmill, stationary bike, resistance machine) most directly answers how astronauts exercise. Exercising two hours daily is also directly relevant. (b) 'The ISS orbits at 17,500 miles per hour' — about speed, not exercise; 'Astronauts see 16 sunrises per day' — about orbital mechanics, not exercise. (c) Sample: 'Do astronauts' bones grow back to normal strength after returning to Earth?' or 'How is the harness treadmill different from a regular treadmill?'

steps: (a) Harness treadmill, stationary bike, resistance machine: specific equipment that directly answers HOW.
Two hours per day: relevant timing detail.
(b) ISS orbital speed: about the station's mechanics, not exercise.
16 sunrises per day: interesting space fact, irrelevant to exercise.
(c) Strong follow-ups address recovery after the mission or technical details of equipment.

Research question: 'What causes the seasons to change on Earth?'

Passage: 'Earth orbits the sun once per year. Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5 degrees. Because of this tilt, different parts of Earth receive more direct sunlight at different times of year. When the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the sun, it receives more direct sunlight and experiences summer, while the Southern Hemisphere has winter. Six months later, the tilt is reversed. Seasons are not caused by how close Earth is to the sun — Earth is actually slightly closer to the sun in January. Earth has one natural satellite, the moon. Mars also has four seasons because it has a similar axial tilt to Earth.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) Earth's axial tilt (23.5 degrees) causing different parts of Earth to receive more or less direct sunlight at different times of year most directly answers the question. The correction that seasons are not caused by distance from the sun is also important. (b) 'Earth has one natural satellite, the moon' — about Earth's moon, not seasons; 'Mars also has four seasons' — about Mars, not about what causes Earth's seasons. (c) Sample: 'Why doesn't the equator have four different seasons?' or 'How would Earth's seasons change if the axis were not tilted?'

steps: (a) Axial tilt causing varied sunlight exposure: the direct cause of seasons.
Seasons not caused by distance (clarification): important conceptual correction.
(b) Earth's moon: unrelated to seasons.
Mars seasons: analogy, but the question asks about Earth.
(c) Good follow-ups explore exceptions (equator) or hypotheticals (no tilt).

Research question: 'How do scientists know how old fossils are?'

Passage: 'Scientists use two main methods to determine a fossil's age. The first method, relative dating, looks at the layers of rock surrounding the fossil — fossils found in deeper layers are generally older. The second method, radiometric dating, measures the decay of radioactive elements in the rock or fossil. Radioactive elements break down at a known rate, so scientists can calculate when the organism lived. The most well-known technique is carbon-14 dating, which works for organisms that lived up to about 50,000 years ago. Fossils older than that require other radioactive elements with longer half-lives. Fossils of trilobites, an ancient sea creature, are among the most common fossils found worldwide.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) Both methods — relative dating (rock layer position) and radiometric dating (measuring radioactive decay at known rates) — most directly answer how scientists know fossil ages. (b) 'Fossils of trilobites are among the most common found worldwide' — about a specific fossil type, not dating methods; 'Carbon-14 works up to 50,000 years ago' — this is a detail about a limitation, less central than describing the two main methods. (c) Sample: 'What radioactive elements are used for dating dinosaur fossils?' or 'Can all fossils be dated using these methods?'

steps: (a) Relative dating (layer position) and radiometric dating (radioactive decay rate): the two core methods.
(b) Trilobites being common fossils: about a specific animal, not dating methods.
Carbon-14 limit (50,000 years): a detail about one specific technique's limitation.
(c) Follow-ups could ask about specific elements used, or limitations for different fossil types.

Research question: 'How do chameleons change their color?'

Passage: 'For a long time, scientists thought chameleons changed color by spreading or concentrating pigment in their skin cells. Recent research has shown that chameleons actually have two layers of special cells called iridophores under their skin. These cells contain tiny crystal structures. When the chameleon relaxes or tenses, the space between the crystals changes, causing the crystals to reflect different wavelengths of light — producing different colors. Chameleons change color mainly to communicate mood and attract mates, not primarily for camouflage. Chameleons have eyes that can move independently of each other. The smallest chameleon species is the Brookesia micra from Madagascar, which can fit on a fingertip.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) The iridophore cells with crystal structures that reflect different light wavelengths when tensed or relaxed most directly explain how chameleons change color. (b) 'Chameleons have eyes that move independently' — about vision, not color change; 'The Brookesia micra can fit on a fingertip' — about size, not color-changing mechanism. (c) Sample: 'How fast can a chameleon change its color?' or 'Do all chameleon species use the same crystal method to change color?'

steps: (a) Iridophore cells with crystals that change spacing to reflect different light: the direct mechanism.
(b) Independent eye movement: about vision ability, not color-change mechanism.
Smallest species size: general biology fact, irrelevant to color change.
(c) Speed or variation across species are natural follow-up questions.

Research question: 'Why do some animals sleep during the day and stay awake at night?'

Passage: 'Animals that are active at night and sleep during the day are called nocturnal. Many nocturnal animals evolved this lifestyle to avoid predators that hunt during daylight hours. Others became nocturnal to avoid competing for food with daytime animals. Some nocturnal animals, like owls and cats, have developed large eyes with pupils that open very wide to gather as much light as possible in the dark. Bats use echolocation to navigate at night. The opposite of nocturnal is diurnal — animals like humans that are active during the day. Some animals are crepuscular, meaning they are most active at dawn and dusk.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) Avoiding predators that hunt during the day, and avoiding competition for food with daytime animals, most directly answer why animals evolved nocturnal habits. (b) 'The opposite of nocturnal is diurnal' — a vocabulary definition, not an explanation of why animals are nocturnal; 'Some animals are crepuscular' — about a different category of behavior, not the reason for nocturnality. (c) Sample: 'How do nocturnal animals find their way in complete darkness?' or 'Which predators do nocturnal animals most often try to avoid?'

steps: (a) Avoiding daytime predators: a direct reason for nocturnality.
Avoiding food competition with daytime animals: another direct reason.
(b) Definition of diurnal: vocabulary, not an explanation of the behavior.
Crepuscular animals: a related but different category, not about why animals are nocturnal.
(c) Follow-ups could explore navigation tools or specific predator-prey relationships.

Research question: 'How does a seed become a plant?'

Passage: 'A seed contains a tiny embryo — the beginning of a new plant — plus stored food to help it grow. When a seed gets enough water, warmth, and oxygen, it begins to germinate. The seed coat breaks open, and a root pushes down into the soil to absorb water and nutrients. Next, a shoot pushes up toward the light. Once the shoot reaches sunlight, the plant grows its first true leaves and begins making its own food through photosynthesis. The time from seed to flowering plant varies widely — some plants flower in a few weeks; others take years. The largest seed in the world is the coco de mer palm seed, which can weigh over 55 pounds.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) The germination sequence — seed needs water, warmth, and oxygen; root grows down; shoot grows up; leaves form and photosynthesis begins — most directly answers how a seed becomes a plant. (b) 'The coco de mer palm seed can weigh over 55 pounds' — about the size of one specific seed, not the germination process; 'Time from seed to flower varies widely' — about timing variation, less central than explaining the actual steps. (c) Sample: 'What happens if a seed does not get enough water to germinate?' or 'How does the seed know which direction is up when it sprouts?'

steps: (a) Germination steps (water/warmth/oxygen trigger; root grows down; shoot grows up; leaves form): the direct process.
(b) Coco de mer weight: interesting extremes but irrelevant to the process.
Variation in flowering time: about timing, not the germination process itself.
(c) Good follow-ups question what happens when conditions are wrong, or explore tropism.

Research question: 'What makes the Dead Sea so salty?'

Passage: 'The Dead Sea is located between Jordan and Israel and sits about 1,400 feet below sea level, making it the lowest point on Earth's land surface. Rivers bring water and dissolved minerals, including salt, into the Dead Sea. However, no rivers flow out of it — the only way water leaves is through evaporation. When the water evaporates, the salt is left behind. Over thousands of years, the salt has built up to extremely high levels — the Dead Sea is about ten times saltier than the ocean. Because of the high salt concentration, no fish can survive in it. Tourists float easily in the Dead Sea because the salt makes the water denser than human bodies.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) Rivers bring salt in but no rivers flow out — only evaporation removes water, leaving salt behind and building up over thousands of years — this most directly answers why the Dead Sea is so salty. (b) 'Tourists float easily because of dense salty water' — about an effect of the saltiness, not the cause; 'The Dead Sea sits about 1,400 feet below sea level' — about elevation, not directly about saltiness. (c) Sample: 'Is the Dead Sea getting saltier over time?' or 'What would happen if a river did flow out of the Dead Sea?'

steps: (a) Inflow of salt via rivers + no outflow + evaporation leaving salt behind = the cause.
(b) Tourists floating: this is a result of the saltiness, not the cause.
1,400 feet below sea level: background geography, not the cause of saltiness.
(c) Follow-ups can explore the trend over time or hypothetical changes to the water cycle.

Research question: 'How does a vaccine help protect people from getting sick?'

Passage: 'Your immune system defends your body against germs by making proteins called antibodies that recognize and attack specific invaders. A vaccine teaches your immune system to recognize a germ without causing the actual disease. Vaccines contain weakened or killed germs, or small pieces of a germ, that are harmless on their own. When your immune system encounters these, it builds antibodies against them. Later, if you are exposed to the real germ, your immune system already knows how to fight it. The first vaccine was developed by Edward Jenner in 1796 for smallpox. Today, vaccines have helped reduce or eliminate many deadly diseases.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) Vaccines contain weakened/killed germs or germ pieces; the immune system builds antibodies against them; when exposed to the real germ later, the immune system is ready — this directly answers how a vaccine protects people. (b) 'Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine in 1796' — historical background, not how vaccines work; 'Vaccines have reduced or eliminated many diseases' — about vaccines' impact, not the mechanism. (c) Sample: 'How long does protection from a vaccine last?' or 'Why do some vaccines require multiple doses?'

steps: (a) Mechanism: weakened/killed germs trigger antibody production; immune system then recognizes the real germ.
(b) History of Jenner: background history, not the working mechanism.
Impact on diseases: results of vaccines, not how they work.
(c) Duration of protection or need for boosters are natural next questions.

Research question: 'How do scientists predict when a hurricane will make landfall?'

Passage: 'Meteorologists use satellite images to track a hurricane's position, size, and movement across the ocean. Weather buoys and aircraft called hurricane hunters fly into storms to measure wind speed, pressure, and temperature. All of this data is fed into powerful computer models that simulate how the storm will move and change. Because hurricanes can shift direction due to changes in surrounding wind patterns, predictions become more accurate the closer the storm gets. The first hurricane of the Atlantic season is given a name beginning with the letter A. Hurricanes draw energy from warm ocean water and weaken when they move over land or colder water.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) Satellites tracking position and movement, hurricane hunters measuring wind/pressure/temperature, and computer models simulating storm movement most directly answer how scientists predict landfall. (b) 'The first hurricane of the season is named with A' — about naming conventions, not prediction methods; 'Hurricanes weaken over land or colder water' — about what weakens hurricanes, not how scientists predict their path. (c) Sample: 'How far in advance can scientists accurately predict where a hurricane will land?' or 'What do hurricane hunter pilots do with the data they collect?'

steps: (a) Satellites, hurricane hunters collecting data, computer models: the prediction toolchain.
(b) Naming convention: administrative, not a prediction method.
What weakens hurricanes: about storm behavior, not prediction methods.
(c) Accuracy timeframe or data use are strong follow-up directions.

Research question: 'How do migrating birds know which direction to fly?'

Passage: 'Scientists have discovered that many migratory birds use several navigation tools at once. Birds can sense Earth's magnetic field and use it like a compass. They also navigate by the stars at night and use the position of the sun during the day. Young birds learn migration routes partly by following experienced adults. Some birds also use landmarks like rivers and mountain ranges. Certain species of birds migrate more than 40,000 miles round trip each year. The Arctic tern holds the record for the longest migration of any animal. Birds have hollow bones, which help reduce their weight for flight.'

(a) Which fact MOST directly answers the research question?
(b) Name TWO facts that are less useful for this question and briefly explain why.
(c) Write ONE follow-up question you would want to research next.
items.answer: (a) Birds sensing Earth's magnetic field, navigating by stars at night and sun during the day, and using landmarks most directly answer how migrating birds know which direction to fly. (b) 'Arctic tern holds the record for longest migration' — about distance records, not navigation mechanism; 'Birds have hollow bones that help with flight' — about flight anatomy, not navigation. (c) Sample: 'How do young birds know to start migrating at the right time of year?' or 'What happens to birds that get separated from their flock during migration?'

steps: (a) Magnetic field sense, star navigation, sun position, landmarks: the multiple navigation methods.
(b) Arctic tern distance record: about a specific species' achievement, not the navigation mechanism.
Hollow bones for flight: about flight mechanics, not directional navigation.
(c) Timing triggers or separation scenarios are good follow-up directions.
